profiles.name: graycrum
profiles.tagline: SHORT GAME MAFIA, APPROACH IS THE SNITCH
profiles.profile: This dude can absolutely rescue a round with the wedges and around-the-green stuff, but the mid-irons keep showing up like they’re late to court and didn’t read the charges. The profile is volatile in the fun, slightly annoying way: one week the short game drags the carcass home, another week the approach play faceplants and the whole card starts smoking. There’s enough pop and enough touch here to make you believe, and then the approach numbers kick the door in and ruin the vibe. When he’s on, it’s scrappy; when he’s off, it’s a bonfire in the fairway.

profiles.name: Leroy4522
profiles.tagline: THE CART IS FASTER THAN THE BALL STRIKING
profiles.profile: This is a long-window grind of somebody who keeps himself just functional enough to stay in the mix while the ball-striking quietly sets fire to the back nine. The tee-and-approach combo is the recurring issue: not a little wonky, properly expensive. The funny part is he can still hang around because the short game and putting occasionally show up like the one sober guy at the party, but they’re usually trying to mop up after a mess already made. It’s the kind of golf that says, “I swear I had a plan,” right before another bogey stack gets built.

profiles.name: derekldavis
profiles.profile: This profile reads like a guy who can keep a round from fully detonating while the tee ball and iron play are busy doing vandalism. The driver isn’t giving him enough help, the approaches aren’t buying him second chances, and the greens are getting visited with all the tenderness of a tax audit. The putter has flashed enough life to suggest he can survive a little chaos, but the underlying shape is still blunt: too few decent looks, too much scrambling, too many holes where the card is just getting kicked in the shins. It’s survival golf, not pretty golf.
